title: Grateful Dead Live at Dane County Coliseum on 1973-10-25
lineage: SBD Master Reel > ? > DAT > CD-R > EAC (secure) > Cool Edit(minor cleanup) > CDWAV > mkwat > SHN

ai_review.summary: A legendary 10/25/73 show with a soaring second set and iconic Dark Star/Eyes/Stella, captured on a decent‑but‑flawed soundboard recording.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely celebrated – the China Cat→Rider segue, the sprawling Dark Star > Mind Left Body Jam > Dark Star, and the transcendent Eyes of the World into Stella Blue are repeatedly highlighted as peak moments.  The soundboard source sounds good for a 1973 tape but suffers from noticeable cuts, occasional hiss, bass clipping and missing sections that temper the listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rave about the musical performance (≈4.6/5) while noting consistent technical flaws that keep the recording quality around a fair level (≈3/5).  Weighted combination yields ~4.2 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Several reviewers mention cuts/patches (especially in Dark Star), missing song segments, tape hiss, occasional pops and bass clipping; however the overall mix is considered decent for a 1973 SBD.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider
Dark Star > Mind Left Body Jam > Dark Star
Weather Report Suite Prelude/Part I/Little India Garden/Go To The River (GDTRFB)
poor_songs: China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider (some versions described as mediocre)
First set overall (noted as weaker and affected by glitches)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set is solid but uneven, with a few glitches; the second set shines, delivering long, exploratory jams that build momentum from China > Rider into Dark Star and then cascade through Eyes, Stella and the Weather Report suite, creating an exhilarating arc.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone and solos are repeatedly praised – especially his work on Dark Star, Eyes of the World and the soulful climax of Stella Blue; vocals described as strong.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass is highlighted for its powerful low end (though some note clipping) and memorable licks at the end of Eyes; a few mention an unusually heavy bass presence during the jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s rhythm guitar and vocal contributions are noted positively, with remarks about his interplay behind Garcia and occasional over‑zealous singing in the Weather Report suite.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard work (Keith Godchaux mainly) receives mixed feedback – some call it magical and supportive, others find moments disjointed or overly plinkety; overall deemed essential to the jam flow.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is praised as tight and energetic, especially on the driving second‑set jams.
